aria: Animated recap of the Hornets' 124 to 112 home win over Cleveland: Royce O'Neale's three with 2:40 left, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Grayson Allen's 27 points, the top scorers, how the Hornets won, and the next game at Phoenix.
notes: Box score from the Hornets' 124–112 home win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Nov 9, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the AP (via Yahoo Sports), Field Level Media, Sports Illustrated's Hornets site, At The Hive and Yardbarker. All 124 Hornets points and all 112 Cavaliers points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals and match Field Level Media's 69–53 halftime score and Yardbarker's 107–80 after three. The 33-point lead is from the AP, Covers and At The Hive; Cleveland's 9-point lead is from Covers and Yardbarker. The 23 threes are Covers' and Sports Illustrated's; points in the paint and fast-break points are Covers'. The end of the six-game losing streak and the first win since Oct. 26 are from the AP. The next game is from the AP and Yardbarker; the Suns' record and the Hornets' standing are from the site's standings.

The play of the game is an original illustration of Royce O'Neale's three from the right wing with 2:40 left, which put Charlotte back up 13 (the AP). Cleveland had cut it to 118–110 on Meleek Thomas' three with under four minutes left; Ryan Kalkbrenner's tip-in and O'Neale's three followed (Field Level Media), and At The Hive calls it the dagger after Kalkbrenner's offensive rebound. The recaps don't describe how he got the shot, so it is drawn as a plain three. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Charlotte Hornets or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to O'Neale's listed 6-foot-6 and 226 pounds (Wikipedia, RealGM), with arms scaled to his reported 6-foot-9 wingspan (Sportskeeda), in the Hornets' home white with No. 00 (Wikipedia). His look hasn't been approved yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
